description: seal-til-block v0 timelock layer (SPEC §7.6), captured LIVE against drand quicknet 2026-06-08. The reveal secret R is timelock-encrypted to a drand round; once that round's BLS signature is published, ANY holder of the round signature recovers R — there is no OC beacon device and no re-wrap endpoint. Given the round's signature (pinned below), timelockDecrypt(tlock) yields R. The tlock blob itself is non-deterministic (IBE randomness), so it is recorded as a captured fixture, not a recomputable expected value.
notes: Captured + verified live (node scripts/seal-demo.mjs proves the full path end-to-end against the live beacon). The round signature is the BLS12-381 group signature over round 29380306, verifiable against the quicknet public_key; it IS the IBE private key for that round. An external `age`/`tle`-compatible decryptor can recover R from a tlock blob given this signature, satisfying invariant #6 (the primary function is callable outside OC code). A colluding drand threshold could compute this signature BEFORE the round's scheduled time, recovering R early — the named, disclosed trust assumption (SECURITY S2).
